`votes.jsonl` is generated by `tools/generate_vote_fixtures.py`, against native
mmx-node commit `ca6438b37c08007106d58efe4a990f6ecb276649`.

The oracle links original `ValidatorVote::is_valid/calc_content_hash` and native
secp256k1 signing. It extracts `Node::get_validators` and `Node::verify_votes`
verbatim, changing the class qualifier. A small harness supplies authenticated
fork flags, validator maps, proof ranking, a controlled clock and publication
capture. Validator-history cases use native header/proof types. Queue cases
deliberately treat proof verification/membership as trusted inputs, independently
of the real work/signature verification tested elsewhere.

110 crypto cases compare the exact raw-domain signing hash, content hash,
acceptance, signature/key parse errors and content-hash short-circuiting. They
include wrong messages/keys/signatures, high-S, zero/overflow scalars and wrong
signature domains. 101 history cases cover unclamped commit delay, history and
validator limits, repeated keys, first-proof selection and missing ancestors.
69 event sequences compare every queued length, accepted publication and fork
vote count, including duplicate and ineligible keys, pending/unverified forks,
strict expiry boundaries, backwards clocks and stronger proofs arriving after
a vote has counted. Ten signed votes reference the actual branch fixtures.

The generator deduplicates identical native header/vote wire blobs with `seed`
and the `queue_wires` dictionary. No expected outcomes are altered. Ordinary
tests need neither C++ nor a reference checkout.
